markdown.headingText: Create the following charts using only R graphics functions. Be sure to customize the charts with your own style/theme.
markdown.markdown:
#### The following data is drawn from an existing dataset in which age, gender, and occupation is collected for each individual along with various metrics regarding sleep quality and other health factors. #### a) Histogram ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load the dataset in R library(readxl) data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Create a histogram for "Sleep Duration" hist(data$`Sleep Duration`, main = "Histogram of Sleep Duration", xlab = "Sleep Duration (hours)", col = "lightblue", border = "black", breaks = 10) # Adjust the number of bins as needed ``` #### b) Bar Chart ##### i. Vertical ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load necessary library to read data library(readxl) library(RColorBrewer) # Read the dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Summarize the data: calculate average quality of sleep sleep_summary <- aggregate(data$`Quality of Sleep`, by = list(data$Occupation), FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE) colnames(sleep_summary) <- c("Occupation", "Avg_Quality_Sleep") # Sort the data for better visualization sleep_summary <- sleep_summary[order(sleep_summary$Avg_Quality_Sleep, decreasing = TRUE), ] # Set font customizations par( family = "serif", # Set font family to serif cex.main = 1.5, # Increase title font size cex.lab = 1.2, # Increase axis title font size cex.axis = 0.8 # Adjust font size for axis labels ) # Create a vertical bar chart barplot( sleep_summary$Avg_Quality_Sleep, names.arg = sleep_summary$Occupation, col = brewer.pal(length(sleep_summary$Occupation), "Dark2"), # Use color scheme for the bars main = "Average Quality of Sleep by Occupation", xlab = "Occupation", ylab = "Average Quality of Sleep (Scale)", las = 2, # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability border = "black", # Add a border around the bars cex.names = 0.8 # Adjust font size for x-axis labels ) # Reset graphical parameters to defaults par(family = "sans", cex.main = 1, cex.lab = 1, cex.axis = 1) ``` ##### ii. Horizontal ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load necessary library to read data library(readxl) # Read the dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Summarize the data: calculate average physical activity level activity_summary <- aggregate(data$`Physical Activity Level`, by = list(data$Occupation), FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE) colnames(activity_summary) <- c("Occupation", "Avg_Physical_Activity") # Sort the data for better visualization activity_summary <- activity_summary[order(activity_summary$Avg_Physical_Activity, decreasing = TRUE), ] # Set font customizations par( family = "serif", # Set the font family to serif cex.main = 1.5, # Increase title size cex.axis = 0.9, # Adjust axis font size cex.lab = 1.2 # Adjust labels font size ) # Create a horizontal bar chart barplot( activity_summary$Avg_Physical_Activity, horiz = TRUE, names.arg = activity_summary$Occupation, col = "chocolate3", # Choose a bar color main = "Average Physical Activity by Occupation", xlab = "Average Minutes per Day", las = 1, # Horizontal axis labels border = "darkgray" # Add borders to bars ) # Reset graphical parameters to defaults par(family = "arial", cex = 1) ``` ##### c) Pie Chart ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load required library for reading data library(readxl) # Replace with the actual path to your dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Summarize data for the "Occupation" variable occupation_counts <- table(data$Occupation) # Set font customizations par( family = "serif", # Set the font family cex.main = 1.5 # Font size for the title ) # Create a pie chart without labels pie( occupation_counts, main = "Distribution of Occupations", col = rainbow(length(occupation_counts)), # Use rainbow colors for slices labels = NA # Remove labels from the slices ) # Add a legend outside the chart legend( "topleft", # Position the legend legend = paste(names(occupation_counts), "(", occupation_counts, ")"), # Legend labels fill = rainbow(length(occupation_counts)), # Colors matching the pie slices bty = "n", # Remove legend border cex = 0.7 # Font size for legend text ) # Reset graphical parameters to default after plotting par(family = "arial", cex = 1) ``` ##### d) Boxplot ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load required library for reading data library(readxl) # Load dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Remove missing values and select relevant columns stress_data <- na.omit(data[, c("Occupation", "Stress Level")]) # Adjust graphical parameters to move the x-axis title downward par(mgp = c(3, 1.5, 0)) # Increase y value to move x-axis title further down # Create a boxplot using base R graphics boxplot( `Stress Level` ~ factor(Occupation), data = stress_data, main = "Boxplot of Stress Levels by Occupation", xlab = "Occupation", ylab = "Stress Level", col = "lightcoral", border = "black", las = 2, # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability cex.axis = 0.8 ) # Reset graphical parameters to default par(mgp = c(4.0, 1, 0)) ``` ##### e) Scatterplot ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load required library for reading data library(readxl) # Read in the dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Summarize data for plotting physical_activity <- data$`Physical Activity Level` quality_of_sleep <- data$`Quality of Sleep` # Set font customizations par( family = "serif", # Set the font family to serif cex.main = 1.5, # Font size for the title cex.lab = 1.2, # Font size for axis labels cex.axis = 1 # Font size for axis tick labels ) # Create a scatter plot with title and customizations plot( physical_activity, quality_of_sleep, main = "Physical Activity Level vs. Quality of Sleep", xlab = "Physical Activity Level", ylab = "Quality of Sleep", pch = 16, # Solid circle points col = "darkturquoise", # Color of the points cex = 1.2 # Size of the points ) # Optionally, add a regression line abline(lm(quality_of_sleep ~ physical_activity), col = "red", lwd = 2) # Reset graphical parameters par(family = "serif", cex.main = 1, cex.lab = 1, cex.axis = 1) ``` ### Repeat using ggplot2, with your own style. #### a) Histogram ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load required libraries library(readxl) library(ggplot2) # Replace with the actual path to your dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Create a ggplot2 histogram for "Sleep Duration" ggplot(data, aes(x = `Sleep Duration`)) + geom_histogram( binwidth = 0.25, # Adjust binwidth as needed fill = "lightblue", color = "black" ) + labs( title = "Histogram of Sleep Duration", x = "Sleep Duration (hours)", y = "Frequency" ) + theme_minimal() + theme( text = element_text(size = 14, family = "serif") # Optional: adjust font size and family ) ``` #### b) Bar Chart ##### i. Vertical ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load necessary libraries library(ggplot2) library(readxl) # Read the dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Summarize the data: calculate average quality of sleep sleep_summary <- aggregate(data$`Quality of Sleep`, by = list(data$Occupation), FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE) colnames(sleep_summary) <- c("Occupation", "Avg_Quality_Sleep") # Sort the data for better visualization sleep_summary <- sleep_summary[order(sleep_summary$Avg_Quality_Sleep, decreasing = TRUE), ] # Create a vertical bar chart ggplot(sleep_summary, aes(x = reorder(Occupation, -Avg_Quality_Sleep), y = Avg_Quality_Sleep, fill = Occupation)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", show.legend = FALSE) + labs( title = "Average Quality of Sleep by Occupation", x = "Occupation", y = "Average Quality of Sleep (Scale)" ) + theme_minimal(base_family = "serif") + theme( plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12), axis.text = element_text(size = 10, angle = 45, hjust = 1) ) + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Paired") ``` ##### ii. Horizontal ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load necessary libraries library(ggplot2) library(readxl) # Read the dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Summarize the data: calculate average physical activity level activity_summary <- aggregate(data$`Physical Activity Level`, by = list(data$Occupation), FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE) colnames(activity_summary) <- c("Occupation", "Avg_Physical_Activity") # Sort the data for better visualization activity_summary <- activity_summary[order(activity_summary$Avg_Physical_Activity, decreasing = TRUE), ] # Create a horizontal bar chart ggplot(activity_summary, aes(x = reorder(Occupation, Avg_Physical_Activity), y = Avg_Physical_Activity, fill = Occupation)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", show.legend = FALSE) + coord_flip() + labs( title = "Average Physical Activity by Occupation", x = "Occupation", y = "Average Minutes per Day" ) + theme_minimal(base_family = "serif") + theme( plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12), axis.text = element_text(size = 10) ) + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") ``` ##### c) Pie Chart ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load required libraries library(readxl) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # Load dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Summarize data for the "Occupation" variable occupation_counts <- data %>% count(Occupation) %>% mutate(Percentage = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) # Ensure all occupations have distinct colors num_occupations <- nrow(occupation_counts) custom_colors <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n = min(12, num_occupations), name = "Set3") # Create the pie chart with ggplot2 (no percentages inside) ggplot(occupation_counts, aes(x = "", y = n, fill = Occupation)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) + coord_polar("y") + labs(title = "Distribution of Occupations") + scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors, labels = paste0(occupation_counts$Occupation, " (", occupation_counts$Percentage, "%)")) + theme_void() + theme( text = element_text(family = "serif"), plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold") ) ``` ##### d) Boxplot ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load required libraries library(ggplot2) library(readxl) # Load dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Remove missing values and select relevant columns stress_data <- na.omit(data[, c("Occupation", "Stress Level")]) # Create the boxplot with ggplot2 and font customizations ggplot(stress_data, aes(x = reorder(Occupation, `Stress Level`), y = `Stress Level`, fill = Occupation)) + geom_boxplot() + labs( title = "Boxplot of Stress Levels by Occupation", x = "Occupation", y = "Stress Level" ) + theme_minimal() + theme( text = element_text(family = "serif"), # Set the font family to serif plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"), # Title customization axis.title = element_text(size = 14), # X and Y axis titles axis.text = element_text(size = 12), # Axis tick text axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1), # Rotate x-axis labels legend.position = "none" # Remove legend for a cleaner look ) + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") # Use a Set2 color palette ``` ##### e) Scatterplot ```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} # Load required library library(readxl) library(ggplot2) # Read in the dataset data <- read_excel("~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~Numbers/Documents/Sleep_health_and_lifestyle_dataset.xlsx") # Create the ggplot scatter plot with customizations ggplot(data, aes(x = `Physical Activity Level`, y = `Quality of Sleep`)) + geom_point(color = "darkturquoise", size = 2) + # Solid points geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red", size = 1.5) + # Regression line labs( title = "Physical Activity Level vs. Quality of Sleep", x = "Physical Activity Level", y = "Quality of Sleep" ) + theme_minimal() + theme( text = element_text(family = "serif"), # Set the font family to serif plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(size = 14), axis.text = element_text(size = 12) ) ```
